object_description: elongated narrow structure along the street with a 117-metre circulation gallery facing the water
geometry_property: all-weather pitch on the gymnasium roof
design_condition: the narrow bar flanks the street with all functional units oriented east towards it and the circulation turned west to the break space and stream, leaving plenty of room for the outdoor areas on the water side

positive: The positioning creates a deliberate two-sidedness between street and break space
The elongated narrow structure accommodates all functions except the gymnasium
A row of trees between street and building shapes the outdoor space and forms a filter layer
The stringent eastern orientation of the classrooms leads to optimal lighting
The equal treatment of all classrooms is appreciated
The access area oriented west over three storeys offers beautiful views and promises a high quality of stay
The gymnasium allows views into it, giving a good spatial connection between the two teaching units
The positioning along the road leaves plenty of space for break and leisure areas on the stream side
These are extremely attractive thanks to an ecological design encouraging play and experiencing nature
The transparency and openness of the building further enhance this impression
The long school body emphasises the street space
The entrance hall accessible from both sides takes up the original connecting axis, creating a new pedestrian axis
The basic layout is very simple and consistently implemented, giving the complex a high degree of clarity
Day structure and kindergartens sit at each end while library and two-storey singing hall are central near the entrance
The corridors in front of the classrooms are well lit
Vertical access is provided by three open staircases at the ends and centre
The all-weather pitch on the gymnasium roof is directly accessible from the upper access zone
A very clear and carefully elaborated design with great strengths in outdoor zoning and spatial relationships
negative: Whether the sometimes unappealing quality of the existing building opposite has been considered remains to be seen
The same question applies to the location of the car parking in the strip of trees
The ground floor orientation offers only an unattractive view of parked cars
The 117-metre access area is very long
The gymnasium interrupts the view to the west
The kindergarten outdoor space to the north is mostly shaded
Despite their spaciousness the long corridors offer too little space for creating learning environments
The additional staircase in the entrance hall appears rather decorative and is not necessary
Whether a natural ventilation low-tech concept is possible with the large west-facing glazing is open to question
The long corridors are rather unusable for lessons with learning landscapes and therefore inefficient
